biography: Olin Galli's journey began on the sun-baked karting tracks of São Paulo, Brazil. Born into a family with limited means, his first taste of speed came from tinkering with a discarded lawnmower engine, which he and his older brother transformed into a makeshift go-kart. It wasn't long before his raw talent caught the eye of a local karting team owner, who offered him a spot in their 2-Stroke 125cc Direct program. Galli quickly rose through the ranks, displaying an innate ability to extract every last ounce of performance from his machine. A defining moment came during the 2015 Brazilian Karting Championship, where he secured a dramatic last-lap victory, solidifying his reputation as a fierce competitor. Now at 33, and considered to be at his peak, Galli is determined to make his mark on the world of motorsports, continuing to hone his skills and chase his ultimate dream of racing on a global stage.
drivingStyle: Galli's driving style is a blend of controlled aggression and calculated risk-taking. He's known for his late-braking maneuvers and willingness to push the limits of grip, often threading the needle between control and chaos. While some criticize his aggressive approach, Galli believes that to win, you must be willing to take chances. He has a natural feel for the car, able to sense the slightest changes in balance and adjust his driving accordingly. Tire management is a work in progress, but he's learning to temper his aggression and preserve his tires for crucial moments in the race.

famousQuote: "Racing isn't just about speed; it's about heart. If you don't have the heart to push past the limit, you'll never truly win."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2015 Brazilian Karting Championship after starting from the back of the grid due to a mechanical failure in qualifying. He overtook 15 karts to claim the victory.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the 2018 Kart 4 championship race due to a mechanical failure, costing him the title.
